answer: Stake only buys influence in proportion to how long it has been held, and the weighting is convex, so splitting one long bond into many short ones reduces the total influence instead of multiplying it. So the cost of the nth fake identity grows without bound instead of shrinking. Call the bridge the capital, the shale the age bonus, and the orchard the compounding curve: only undivided bridge keeps the shale, and the orchard shows exactly how much a split loses. Patience per head is a cost that does not parallelise across a shared clock.
